facts.text: Vehicle-in-the-loop (VIL) testing drives a complete real machine in a safe, empty test area while virtual hazards are fed to its sensors or controller to trigger real braking.
facts.quote: Vehicle-in-the-loop testing drives the complete real machine on a safe, empty test area while virtual hazards are fed to its sensors or controller

facts.text: VIL sends simulated detections to the real braking system through injection or over-the-air stimulation and feeds the machine's real position and speed back into the simulation to align subsequent stimuli.
facts.quote: the simulated detection reaches the braking system by injection or over-the-air stimulation, the machine really brakes, and its real position and speed are fed back into the simulation so that the next stimuli match.

facts.text: VIL is also called mixed reality or augmented-reality testing because a real machine moves through an empty area while reacting to virtual objects.
facts.quote: Because the machine moves through an empty area while reacting to virtual objects, this is also called mixed reality or augmented-reality testing

facts.text: One cited on-road VIL approach injects virtual hazards into a real vehicle's controller on a test track.
facts.quote: one cited approach injects virtual hazards into a real vehicle's controller on a test track

facts.text: An augmented-reality proving-ground platform was published in 2024; the passage identifies the VIL evidence as on-road only.
facts.quote: an augmented-reality proving-ground platform was published in 2024 [Chapter 1].

facts.text: VIL proves real braking dynamics, actuator and controller delays, end-to-end latency, and the real operator interface without endangering people or targets, providing a bridge between simulation and field testing.
facts.quote: VIL proves real braking dynamics, real actuator and controller delays, real end-to-end latency and the real operator interface without endangering people or targets; "it is the bridge between simulation and field"

facts.text: VIL cannot prove perception of injected objects unless the objects are stimulated over the air.
facts.quote: It cannot prove perception of the injected objects unless they are stimulated over the air

facts.text: A test bench cannot reproduce soft soil, grades, sinkage, articulated dynamics, payload behavior, vibration, dust or weather.
facts.quote: a bench cannot reproduce soft soil, grades, sinkage, articulated dynamics, payload behavior, vibration, dust or weather

facts.text: The size of heavy machines makes VIL facilities difficult.
facts.quote: the size of heavy machines makes facilities difficult [Chapter 7].

facts.text: A 2024 survey of on-road VIL evidence reports limitations in testbench fidelity, multi-target radar simulation, multi-camera systems and especially lidar stimulation.
facts.quote: A 2024 survey reports limitations in testbench fidelity, multi-target radar simulation, multi-camera systems and especially lidar stimulation

facts.text: A 2024 survey of on-road VIL evidence did not identify a full-scale VIL platform ready for comprehensive industrial testing.
facts.quote: A 2024 survey reports limitations in testbench fidelity, multi-target radar simulation, multi-camera systems and especially lidar stimulation, and did not identify a full-scale VIL platform ready for comprehensive industrial testing

facts.text: Off-road VIL on production-scale haul trucks, loaders, dozers or excavators was not found; the available VIL evidence is on-road only.
facts.quote: off-road VIL on production-scale haul trucks, loaders, dozers or excavators was not found [Chapters 1, 7].

facts.text: The booklet recommends using VIL only where its extra physical fidelity justifies the investment.
facts.quote: The booklet's hierarchy uses VIL "only where its extra physical fidelity justifies the investment"

facts.text: The booklet treats VIL as emerging and capital-intensive rather than a proven shortcut for heavy machines.
facts.quote: treats it as emerging and capital-intensive rather than a proven shortcut for heavy machines [Chapter 1].
